title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages of the 1986 notes 'Algèbre des figures'). A 'figure' F is a set of subsets of an ambient set L. Its support is |F| = union of the elements of F. The defining condition is that every point x of |F| lies in a smallest element of F. Each A in F then has a 'stratum' A° = A minus the union of the elements of F strictly contained in A. The strata partition |F|, and the figure is an abstract combinatorial stratified space. Three relations are used:
- F' ≪ F: F' refines F. Each A in F' lies in a smallest element of F, and A∩B is a union of strata of F' for every B in F.
- F' ≼ F: F' is a subdivision of F, i.e. a refinement with |F'| = |F|.
- F' ≤ F: F' is a closed subfigure of F, i.e. F' ⊂ F and F' is downward closed.

Page 28 constructed the infimum F.G of F and G for ≪. Its elements are the sets A∩B (A in F, B in G) with A°∩B° ≠ ∅, and |F.G| = |F|∩|G|.

This page proves that the product F.G is monotone in each variable for all three relations:
- (a) F' ≪ F ⇒ F'.G ≪ F.G. This is trivial from the definition of F.G as an infimum.
- (b) F' ≼ F ⇒ F'.G ≼ F.G. This follows from (a) plus the equality of supports.
- (c) F' ≤ F ⇒ F'.G ≤ F.G. It is made explicit as F'.G = {C in F.G | C ⊂ |F'|}.

Proof of (c), in two steps:
1. Inclusion F'.G ⊂ F.G. Because F' is downward closed in F, the stratum A° of A in F' equals its stratum in F. So the condition A°∩B° ≠ ∅ is the same in both, and F'.G ⊂ F.G.
2. Closedness. Suppose A'∩B' (A' in F, B' in G) is in F.G and is contained in some A∩B in F'.G. The 'theory of F.G' says that inclusion of such intersections forces A' ⊂ A and B' ⊂ B. Indeed, a point of A'°∩B'° lies in A, and A' is the smallest element containing it. Hence A' is in F', because F' is closed in F.

Corollary: axiom C6 holds. In the margin this reads: for G ≤ F and F' ≼ F, the induced G' := F'.G satisfies G' ≼ G and G' ≤ F'. So subdivisions pull back along closed subfigures. The margin also isolates two auxiliary lemmas on chains P ≪ Q ≪ R. Roughly, if P ≼ R then P ≼ Q and Q ≼ R; and if P ≤ R then P ≤ Q.

Axiom C7 (extension of subdivisions): given G ≤ F and a subdivision G' ≼ G, there is a subdivision F' ≼ F inducing G' on G. Grothendieck takes the disjoint union F' = G' ∪ (F \ G). He then lists what must be checked: (a) F' is a figure, (b) F' subdivides F, (c) F' induces G' on G. Page 30 carries out these checks.

Purpose: an axiomatic 'algebra of figures' with closed inclusions and subdivisions playing roles like cofibrations and weak equivalences. It is presumably meant as an elementary or tame model of stratified/polyhedral geometry.
errors: Minor gap: the step 'A'∩B' ⊂ A∩B ⇒ A' ⊂ A, B' ⊂ B' is quoted from 'the theory of F.G' rather than proved here. It holds because A'°∩B'° ≠ ∅ and A' is the smallest element of F containing any point of A'°.
The margin lemma on chains P ≪ Q ≪ R is stated hesitantly with crossed-out alternatives. Its exact hypotheses (e.g. whether equality of supports is needed) are not pinned down on this page.
The explicitation F'.G = {C ∈ F.G | C ⊂ |F'|} is asserted without proof. It is plausible, since C = A∩B ⊂ |F'| with C° meeting A° forces A ∈ F' by downward closure.

ideas.what: Monotonicity of the infimum (common refinement) F.G of stratified 'figures' with respect to refinement, subdivision and closed-subfigure relations
ideas.modern_name: functoriality of common refinement / intersection of stratifications; meet in a poset of cell decompositions
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore of PL topology and o-minimal cell decomposition

ideas.what: Axiom C6: subdivisions restrict along closed subfigures (G' = F'.G is a subdivision of G and a closed subfigure of F')
ideas.modern_name: base change of weak equivalences along cofibrations / restriction of subdivisions to subcomplexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: PL topology folklore; abstractly Waldhausen / Brown cofibration-category axioms

ideas.what: Axiom C7: any subdivision of a closed subfigure extends to a subdivision of the whole figure, via F' = G' ∪ (F\G)
ideas.modern_name: extension of subdivisions from a subcomplex (cf. extension lemmas in PL topology; gluing axiom in cofibration categories)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL topology (Whitehead, Zeeman) in the cellular setting

missed.claim: The axioms C6/C7 are an early axiomatisation of stratified spaces in which closed subfigures act like cofibrations and subdivisions like weak equivalences. This is close in spirit to cofibration categories and to the program of 'topologie modérée' in the Esquisse. Because figures are not required to be cells, extending a subdivision is trivial (F' = G' ∪ (F\G)), unlike in the PL setting.
missed.quote: Vérifions maintenant C7 : G ≤ F ∃ subdivision F' de F qui induise G'. On prend F' = G' ∪ (F\G)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor documentary point. It shows how Grothendieck tried to axiomatise tame/stratified geometry in 1986, of possible interest to historians of the Esquisse's tame-topology program. The mathematics itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary, correct verifications of monotonicity and two axioms in an unpublished axiomatic 'algebra of figures'. The only interest is historical: the C-axioms suggest an abstract framework for tame stratified geometry, but nothing on this page is mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: '(trivial par all[?] de ≪ comme [?])' is likely '(trivial par déf. de ≪ comme Inf)'.
'et un fermé dans F.G' should read 'et est fermé dans F.G'.
'(C'est un ensemble disjoint[?])' is likely '(c'est une réunion disjointe)'.
'(d'après le théorème de F.G)' may be '(d'après la théorie de F.G)'.
In the margin, the second chain lemma likely reads 'b) P ≪ Q ≪ R et P ≤ R ⇒ P ≤ Q', with 'Q ≤ R' crossed out.
'b) que [-...-] subdivise F' should read 'b) que ça subdivise F', and 'c) qui induit G' sur G' should read 'c) qu'il induit G' sur G'.
